subject: math

objective.text: Pair objects and skip-count to relate to even numbers.

explanations.title: Pair to test even
explanations.text: Pair up the objects. If every object has a match, the number is even. If one is left over, the number is not even.

source_ref.section: Concept Development (S: every counter had a partner)

explanations.title: Skip-count by twos
explanations.text: Even numbers are the numbers we say when we count by twos. We say 2, 4, 6, 8. We do not say 3 or 7.

source_ref.section: Concept Development (S: we don't say 3 when we count by twos)

explanations.title: Doubles are even
explanations.text: Doubling a whole number gives an even number. 7 plus 7 equals 14. 14 is even. 3 plus 4 equals 7 is not a double, so 7 is not even.

explanations.title: Zero is even
explanations.text: 0 plus 0 equals 0. It is a doubles fact. We also say 0 when we count by twos. So 0 is even.

examples.title: 2 is even
examples.text: Two children stand side by side. Each has a match. 1 plus 1 equals 2. 2 is even.

examples.title: 3 is not even
examples.text: Three children line up. The third child has no match. 3 is not even.

examples.title: 7 and 14
examples.text: 7 counters: one is left over, so 7 is not even. 7 more counters make 14. Every counter has a match, so 14 is even.
